_comment: The iTop branches this extension claims to support, and the PHP versions each is
tested on. This file is the single source of truth: the CI matrix is computed from
it, and every prose copy of the claim should be checked against it rather than
maintained beside it.
If the README, a Hub listing or extension.xml's <description> restate this claim in
prose, delimit the markdown copies with a supported-versions:begin/end pair and add a
test - modelled on altioo-mcp's ModuleMetadataTest::testProseAgreesWithTheDeclaredSupport
- that reads them against this file and composer.json's PHP range, and fails on any
disagreement. Edit here, not there.
A branch names a minor (3.2), never a patch. CI resolves the latest patch of that
branch at run time, so a new 3.2.x published by Combodo is exercised by the next
scheduled run without anyone editing anything - which is the point: the version a
poorly-tested extension breaks on is usually the one released after anyone last looked.
branch           the iTop minor, as it appears in the tag names of Combodo/iTop
php              PHP versions to install that branch on. Two is enough: the floor
and the ceiling of what composer.json allows. The middle version
is covered by the unit matrix in ci.yml.
allow_prerelease resolve to an alpha/beta/rc when the branch has no stable patch
yet. True for a branch you intend to support at its GA and want to
be told about early; never for one users are already running.
pin              an exact release - 3.2.1, or 3.2.1-1 for one re-spin of it - when
a resolved patch is known broken and the failure is not this
extension's. It is what gets installed, not only what is reported.
Temporary by nature: say why, in this file.
Add a branch only once it has actually been installed on - the whole matrix, on the
floor and the ceiling of the PHP range, not a spot check. A branch named here is a
branch every prose copy tells an operator is tested; naming one that is not is the
single thing this file exists to prevent. allow_prerelease is there for the first look
at a branch; the entry comes after the run, not before it.
